parsed.process: Cocoon sorting before industrial silk reeling
parsed.current_inefficiency: Sorting is the most labor-intensive reeling step, and RGB-vision sorters only judge the cocoon's external shell — they cannot see internal state (live vs. dead pupa, double pupae, or Uzi-fly larva/exit damage hidden under intact silk)
parsed.ai_technique: Impact-acoustic emission sensing + 1D-CNN classifier (the same vibro-acoustic tap-test pipeline used for egg-crack and nut-emptiness detection)
parsed.how_it_improves: A singulation rig drops each cocoon onto/past a light tapper while a contact piezo or MEMS microphone records the impact ringdown (a few ms waveform). The waveform (or its spectrogram) is fed to a 1D-CNN/spectrogram-CNN trained on labeled cocoons; resonant frequency and damping encode internal mass and cavity — empty/Uzi-exited shells ring higher/longer, double-pupa cocoons are heavier/lower, dead-pupa (disease) cocoons damp differently. Output is a per-cocoon class that drives a pneumatic diverter, catching internal defects vision misses and cutting manual back-checking
parsed.why_not_done_before: Sericulture vision research has converged almost entirely on RGB/CNN external grading; acoustic tap-testing needs a custom mechanical singulation+tapper rig and a hand-labeled acoustic dataset (requiring destructive ground-truth dissection of pupae), which is rarely built for a low-margin crop concentrated in regions with cheap manual labor
parsed.primary_quote: automatization is mandatory to reduce silk costs

reasoning_trace.reasoning: AI penetration here is HIGH but it is almost all RGB computer vision, which is fundamentally blind to what is inside an intact, opaque silk shell — exactly where double-pupae, dead/diseased pupae, and Uzi-fly internal damage live. Impact-acoustic + 1D-CNN is a mature, proven technique for non-destructive internal-state inspection (egg cracks, hollow nuts, fruit firmness), so it is feasible off-the-shelf and attacks the dimension vision cannot reach. I rejected hyperspectral/NIR (penetrates only mm of silk, weaker at deep internal mass differences and far costlier per lane) in favor of cheap piezo/MEMS acoustics that directly sense mass and cavity resonance
reasoning_trace.decision: Use impact-acoustic ringdown + 1D-CNN to classify each singulated cocoon by internal state and divert defects vision-based sorters miss
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - the ML and sensors are off-the-shelf, but reliable singulation throughput and acoustic ground-truth labeling are real engineering risks
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: the silk shell's heavy acoustic damping flattens the resonant differences between live, dead, and Uzi-exited pupae below detectable SNR, or a vendor has already shipped acoustic/weight-based internal cocoon sorting that I'm unaware of
